Summary: evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity + autoscaling behavior. Zenith runs latency-sensitive real-time transaction scoring / fraud decisions (sub-100ms median, 99th pctile target <200ms) and chat-support for VIP merchants. They want reserved GPU planning with throughput guarantees for peak windows (US business hours + batch night jobs).

Key requirements / asks: 
- Guaranteed throughput (tokens/sec / rps) and predictable P50/P95/P99 latency SLOs for Dedicated pools. Want contractual SLA on availability and latency fallback plan.
- Autoscaling policy review: scale-up latency, scale-down cooldown, min active instances (warm-pool) vs cost tradeoff. Prefer warm-pool for models with KV cache warm-up concerns.
- Warm pools: want ability to keep small number of warmed GPUs per model variant in each region; cost vs latency analysis requested.
- Queueing behavior: want clear docs on request queuing, backpressure, priority routing for VIP merchants, max queue length and behavior under overload.
- Reserved GPU planning: sizing guidance for sustained throughput, burst capacity options, and lighting-fast scale-up for traffic spikes (flash sales).
- SLA negotiation points: remedies for missed latency SLOs, runbook for failover to cheaper model variants, routing policies across regions.
